business.description: Shankar Lal Rampal Dye-Chem Limited is a trading-led company transitioning to an integrated manufacturing enterprise, dealing in textile chemicals, dyes, pigments, and home and cleaning care products such as dish wash gel, fabric wash liquid, floor cleaner, toilet cleaner, glass cleaner, hand wash, and detergent powder.

outlook.statement: Global textile chemicals market valued at USD 31.81 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 50.84 billion by 2034 at CAGR 5.35%. Global dyes and pigments market valued at USD 34.8 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 51.2 billion by 2035 at CAGR ~3.0%. India's chemicals industry valued at Rs. 21,50,750 crore (US$ 250 billion) in 2024, expected to reach Rs. 35,26,800–39,67,650 crore (US$ 400–450 billion) by 2030 and Rs. 86,03,000 crore (US$ 1 trillion) by 2040 at CAGR ~9–10%. India's textile industry expanded to nearly Rs. 16.66 lakh crore (US$ 190 billion) in 2025-26, targeting Rs. 33.10 lakh crore (US$ 350 billion) by 2030. Specialty chemicals net exports projected to grow over tenfold by 2040 from US$ 2 billion in 2021 to US$ 21 billion. World Bank reaffirmed India's FY 2026-27 GDP growth forecast at 6.6%. IMF raised India's GDP growth forecast for FY 2026-27 citing strong domestic momentum and easing US tariff pressure. Rajasthan GSDP projected at Rs. 18.75 lakh crore (US$ 213.21 billion) in FY26, CAGR 10.65% between FY16-FY26.

Company transitioning from trading-led model to integrated manufacturing via backward integration at Suwana, Bhilwara for home and cleaning care products to cut reliance on third-party suppliers, build secure supply chain, enable margin expansion, broader product mix, and long-term scalable growth. Investing in modern blending systems, automated packaging, and green chemistry (low-VOC, biodegradable, water-efficient formulations). Focus on resilient domestic market and diversification to reduce reliance on single external market or trade corridor.

The Company's continued focus on sanitization and home care chemicals — categories seeing sustained demand on the back of rising hygiene and cleanliness awareness — is expected to provide meaningful growth opportunities going forward, offering revenue streams that serve both public health needs and the Company's diversification objectives.
With robust underlying demand for its products and a clear roadmap toward integrated manufacturing, the Company is well positioned to add capacity and sustain growth in the years ahead.

Considering the Company's existing foothold/experience in the Dyes and Chemical sector, established & diversified client base, association with various agents, it's competent sales team and an established marketing setup, it does not foresee any problem in marketing its production.

risks: Raw material and energy cost volatility pressuring margins
Dependence on third-party suppliers under trading model limiting control over availability, quality, delivery timelines
Thin and volatile trading margins sensitive to competitive pricing and market swings
Price transparency and competitive pressure limiting pricing power
Working capital intensity from inventory holding and credit extension sensitive to receivables cycles and interest rates
Currency and logistics exposure from imported goods affecting landed cost and delivery timelines
Rising sustainability and regulatory expectations (eco-friendly, low-VOC, biodegradable formulations)
Execution risk in manufacturing transition: project execution, technology adoption, market-entry risk
Global economic and trade uncertainty: moderating global economy, energy price volatility, shifting trade patterns
Anti-dumping duties on material imports in Europe and stricter environmental compliance norms reshaping production economics
Complexities in the dye-chemical and allied sectors
The Company is a trading company; hence, no hedging of raw material is required. Hedging products are not available for the major chemicals purchased by the Company.
Exposure of the Company to commodity and commodity risks faced throughout the year: not applicable
Foreign exchange risks are tracked and managed within the risk management framework. Short-term foreign currency asset-liability mismatch is continuously monitored and hedged.
